name: polynomial-roots
description: Polynomial Roots — every root of every polynomial whose coefficients come from a small finite alphabet, painted by density. The picture at the head of Baez–Christensen–Derbyshire's "The Beauty of Roots": for the Littlewood alphabet {−1, +1} at degree 24 that is 2^24 polynomials and ~400 million roots, with holes at the roots of unity, a line along the real axis, a dense ring at the unit circle (Bousch), and dragon curves inside the disk. An explorer (alphabet, degree scrub, density and degree colour, pan/zoom, permalink, PNG) plus a gallery of named phenomena from the literature. Established by ADR-0046; the root engine is an app-local Aberth–Ehrlich solver in a worker pool splatting per-degree density into float textures, pinned in the node gate against @cas/core's Durand–Kerner. Built on the shared @cas/* packages — @cas/ui (browser shell, fatal boundary, accessible canvas), @cas/gpu (WebGL2 shader substrate, colour ramps, the shared histogram-equalisation tone map), @cas/core (the golden root-finder), @cas/flow (the pan/zoom view transform), @cas/interchange (#vs= permalinks) and @cas/export (PNG figure metadata). No new package (ADR-0007); honest labelling — the picture is ≈ at a finite degree, and only cited theorems read as theorems.
author: Andrew Graven <andrew@graven.com>
